title: The Pacifier
full_review:
"The Pacifier" (Disney) is anything but pacifying.

In this embarrassingly unfunny comedy directed by Adam Shankman, Vin Diesel plays Shane Wolfe, a tough-guy Navy SEAL assigned to baby-sit the five children of an assassinated government scientist while simultaneously searching their suburban home for their late father's top-secret computer program, with the fate of the free world -- and the Girl Scout cookie drive -- hanging in the balance.

Before his tour of domestic duty is done, Shane not only saves the day by thwarting an onslaught of ninja-clad terrorists, but in the process manages to bring the family closer together and connect with his inner nanny.

Clumsily acted and directed, this laugh-free riff on "Kindergarten Cop," "Daddy Daycare" and countless others -- though not without some sentiment -- reeks more than the many diapers its brooding star changes throughout the film.

Some action violence, recurring crude and potty humor, occasional mild rude language, and several sequences of children in peril. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-II -- adults and adolescents. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG -- parental guidance suggested.
